security_problem: Round-4 P1/P2: the stdio identity resolver hashes every regular-file argument, so mutable runtime data arguments (logs, databases, datasets, output paths) change the digest and cause false-deny on legitimate undeclared file args; and the proxy resolves invocation identity even for a logical server with no attestation, doing wasted startup work that can read a large sparse data file.
required_behavior: A configured stdio invocation digest always binds the locally resolved launcher executable and every literal argv value in order; only policy-declared entry argument positions (attestation.entry_arg_positions, zero-based indexes into ServerArgs excluding the executable) bind the resolved local regular-file content. Omitted/empty positions mean launcher + literal argv only. Loader rejects negative and duplicate positions; resolver rejects out-of-range, missing, symlink-failure, non-regular, and read-failure declared entries; declared positions are normalized by sorting a copy so YAML list order is not part of identity; no inference or fallback scanning of undeclared file args. A logical server with no attestation performs zero identity-resolution work in both New and NewWithTracing. A hot reload introducing a pin resolves before the runtime barrier and publishes policy plus prepared identity atomically; resolution failure publishes the configured pin with unresolved identity and the next tools/call fails closed; removing a pin clears the verdict; reintroduction resolves again. All 11 canonical registry-runner rejects, negative controls, approval/taint snapshots, and entry-artifact-not-transitive boundary are preserved.
failure_behavior: Fail closed for tools/call when attestation is configured and identity resolution is missing, unsupported, or mismatched; never hash or open undeclared file arguments; never perform resolver work without a configured pin.
